raw:
{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging" },
  "read": "The students who skipped the reading know the room knows, and that public exposure is the real sting — they look like they cannot or do not pull their weight. The students who did the reading feel used, which turns into resentment that poisons the group. Both halves need to feel capable and like legitimate members of this community, and right now neither fully does.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Call out who clearly did not read, assign a grade consequence on the spot, or shame the unprepared half publicly — which hardens their avoidance next time and convinces them the class is a place where they lose status, not gain it." },
  "mentorMove": "Pause the discussion, name the pattern honestly without pointing fingers, and rebuild the expectation as a shared responsibility to the group — so coming prepared is framed as mattering to your peers, not just pleasing the teacher.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "Everyone reads before discussion — that standard is not moving.",
    "Discussion is a collective obligation, not a spectator sport where some carry others."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Offer a two-minute silent re-read or annotation at the start of class so unprepared students can get a foothold before the conversation opens.",
    "Let students choose how they contribute — a written question, a connection, a pushback — so there are multiple credible entry points beyond just having read every word."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, let me stop us for a second — not to call anyone out, but because I can feel the energy shifting in here, and I think we all feel it." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "When some people come in prepared and others do not, what does that actually do to the conversation for everyone? Think about it from both sides for a moment." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I want us to figure out together: the reading is not optional, because the people in this room are your thinking partners and they cannot do their best work without you in it. So what would make it more likely that everyone actually shows up ready? I am genuinely asking — I want to hear what is getting in the way and what would help." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding all of you to this because I have high standards for what this class can be, and I have seen enough from every one of you to know you can meet them. Coming prepared is how you show your people in this room that they matter to you — and how you make sure you matter back. That is the standard, and I believe we can get there together." }
  ],
  "longGame": "If the group builds a brief norm together — even something small, like a one-sentence written reaction due before class — ownership shifts from compliance to community, and the kids who were coasting start to feel the pull of belonging to something rather than the fear of a grade."
}
situation: Half the class did the reading and half clearly did not, and the half that did is getting visibly annoyed at carrying discussions.
